slides.heading: A stronger model for *75% less compute*
paras: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman told employees at a town hall on Thursday that MAI-Base-2 is a stronger pre-trained model than the one powering OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol.
"We used one-quarter of the compute that OpenAI used to train their model," he said, according to Business Insider.

slides.heading: Secretly tested against *OpenAI's Spud*
paras: Suleyman said Microsoft "privately and confidentially" compared MAI-Base-2 with OpenAI models, including one nicknamed Spud that he said powers GPT-5.6.
He said Microsoft's model scored better on tests of how well an AI understands and predicts patterns in information. He also claimed it used 12 times less compute than DeepSeek.

slides.heading: Partners on paper, *rivals in practice*
paras: Microsoft has invested billions in OpenAI and holds a stake likely worth more than $100 billion. The two still work together on Azure and Copilot, but the relationship has frayed.
In March, Microsoft reassigned Suleyman to focus on building its own AI models in its superintelligence unit.

paras.t: The results come from Microsoft's own internal tests. OpenAI did not respond to Business Insider.

slides.hook: Microsoft is now racing the AI lab it helped build. Follow to see if MAI-Base-2 lives up to the claim.
